Actor.description:
Who wrote a record or acted: the session, the program, the person and
the agent's name, each when known, and at least one. Every record type that names who
acted holds one.

agent.description:
The name the agent was given, such as `nightly scheduler`, as
free text.

person.description: The person who acted, such as `luke`, or their email address.

program.description: The program that acted, such as `claude-code` or `codex`.

description:
`tasks/task/v2`: the frontmatter of a Markdown task under `tasks/`, whose body holds its prose.

`defer` hides the task until a date, a date-time or a horizon after `reviewed`.
`after` references the tasks in the same repo that it waits on. `repeat`
names when a repeating task comes back, and `ephemeral` that a missed day
is not kept. `from_hour` is the hour of the person's day it is available
from. `contexts` tags where it can be done. `reviewed` is the day it was
last looked at. `owner` names the agent or person who holds it, such as a
session id or a handle. `parent` references the task in the same repo that
this one is part of, and `kind` says whether it is a `task`, as when it is
left out, or a `project`, whose `brief` may reference a brief such as a
README.md. Any other field, such as Reflect's `id` and `pinned`, is
admitted and ignored.
title: Task
